CSIR-Indian Institute of Petroleum (CSIR-IIP), Dehradun, in collaboration with CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI) and CSIR-Advanced Materials and Processes Research Institute (CSIR-AMPRI), showcased Bio-Binder Technology during a technology demonstration programme aimed at accelerating the commercialization of indigenous green technologies for sustainable road infrastructure. The event brought together senior scientists, industry leaders and research collaborators to promote technology-led national development and sustainable innovation.

Palla and his team from CSIR-IIP; Dr. G. Bharath and his team from CSIR-CRRI; along with representatives from industry collaborating with CSIR-IIP and CSIR-CRRI for the commercial scale-up and deployment of Bio-Binder technology.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. Harender Singh Bisht said that Bio-Binder Technology represents a significant advancement towards sustainable road construction by converting agricultural and biomass waste into an environmentally friendly substitute for petroleum-derived bitumen. He stated that the technology reflects the collective efforts of the three CSIR laboratories to reduce dependence on imported petroleum products, promote the effective utilization of agricultural residues, create additional income opportunities for farmers and contribute to India's transition towards greener and more sustainable infrastructure.
Speaking on the occasion, Dr. C. Ravi Sekhar highlighted that India's rapidly expanding road infrastructure continues to depend heavily on imported bitumen. He said that the Bio-Binder technology provides an indigenous and sustainable alternative by converting agricultural residues, particularly rice straw and other biomass waste, through pyrolysis into valuable products such as bio-oil, bio-binder, biochar and biogas. Committee deliberates on Strengthening Human–Wildlife Conflict Mitigation through Technology, Community Participation and Coordinated National Action
The Parliamentary Consultative Committee of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change met today in New Delhi, under the Chairmanship of the Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav. The agenda of the meeting was to deliberate on the issue of Human–Wildlife Conflict (HWC) and the measures required for strengthening prevention, mitigation and long-term coexistence between people and wildlife. Dignitaries in attendance included Union Minister of State (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, along with Members of Parliament as part of the Committee, besides senior officers of the Ministry, PCCFs and Chief Wild Life Wardens of participating States.
The Committee was apprised of the follow-up action taken on the directions issued during its previous meeting held on 18.12.2025. These included consultations by States and Union Territories with Members of Parliament from conflict-affected areas. During the meeting, the Ministry highlighted that conflict patterns vary across landscapes, with human–elephant conflict being predominant in several States, while conflicts involving tigers, leopards, bears, rhinoceroses, wild boars, gaurs, primates and other species require location-specific management approaches.
The Committee was informed about the establishment of the Centre of Excellence on Human–Wildlife Conflict (CoE-HWC) at SACON, WII South Centre, Coimbatore, announced by the Prime Minister of India, during the 7 th National Board for Wildlife meeting. The Centre has been established as a national institution for scientific research, technological innovation, policy support, capacity building and community-centred approaches for effective management of human–wildlife conflict. The Committee also noted the launch of the National Human–Wildlife Conflict Portal on 10.07.2026, as a unified digital platform for recording conflict incidents, data management, knowledge sharing and decision support. Further, it was informed that the Regional Action Plan (RAP) on Elephant Conservation for South India has been approved.
Presentations were made by the States of Assam, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh , highlighting their conflict scenarios, mitigation measures, community participation initiatives, use of technology, institutional mechanisms and recommendations for strengthening national efforts. The experiences presented underscored the importance of landscape-specific planning, rapid response systems, habitat improvement, protection of wildlife corridors, scientific monitoring, early warning systems, community engagement and inter-State coordination.
The discussions emphasised that effective management of human–wildlife conflict requires an integrated approach combining ecological conservation with protection of human lives and livelihoods.

articles.full_content:
Sustainable energy infrastructure plays a vital role in promoting economic development while ensuring environmental conservation. Through timely institutional support, many entrepreneurs are contributing towards India's renewable energy transition.
One such inspiring example is Palnadu Solar Power Pvt. Ltd. , a renewable energy enterprise established by Ms. Sujatha Seelam in Guntur, Andhra Pradesh. The company's journey demonstrates the transformative impact of the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in supporting Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to build sustainable businesses.
Palnadu Solar Power Pvt. Ltd. established a 5.5 MW grid-connected solar power plant to generate clean and sustainable electricity, helping meet the growing power requirements of the region while contributing to India's renewable energy goals. Recognising the project's long-term potential, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes extended financial assistance of ₹ 15 crore in 2015 through Venture Capital (Equity with Optionally Convertible Debentures) , enabling the successful establishment and commissioning of the solar power project.
5.5 MW Grid-Connected Solar Power Plant
The financial assistance enabled the enterprise to establish a modern solar power generation facility that is successfully supplying clean energy while strengthening the company's financial position. The project has generated direct and indirect employment opportunities for local communities, established strong market linkages with clients, and contributed towards sustainable rural development through reliable renewable energy generation.
The project has emerged as a successful model of clean energy entrepreneurship by creating valuable renewable energy infrastructure and promoting environmentally sustainable development. Through reliable solar power generation, the enterprise is supporting rural power requirements while creating livelihood opportunities and contributing to India's transition towards green energy.
Reflecting on the journey, Ms. Sujatha Seelam said:
"The timely and concessional financial support received under VCF-SC enabled us to set up a 5.5 MW solar plant at Vijayawada. Today, Palnadu Solar is supporting the rural power requirement along with multiple job opportunities at the village level."

Ltd. demonstrates how targeted financial assistance under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castates (VCF-SC) is empowering Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to invest in renewable energy and sustainable infrastructure. By enabling access to concessional finance, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to promote entrepreneurship, generate employment, strengthen rural economies, and contribute to India's vision of a cleaner, greener and more sustainable future.

PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Adds One Lakh Beneficiary Households Every Six Days July 2026 Records Highest-Ever Monthly Rooftop Solar Installations under the Scheme Nearly 19 lakh households now receiving zero electricity bills; 14.8 GW rooftop solar capacity commissioned so far Over 25,000 Central Government Buildings Solarized under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana has crossed a landmark milestone with over 50.06 lakh households now benefiting from rooftop solar installations across the country.
Achieved in just over two years since its launch, this milestone marks a significant acceleration compared to the 7.94 lakh rooftop solar installations recorded over the previous ten years. It reflects the rapid implementation of the world's largest rooftop solar programme, with an outlay of ₹75,021 crore. The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana is Government of India's flagship rooftop solar scheme under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the scheme is today benefiting 1 lakh households every six days, making it one of the fastest growing clean energy programmes anywhere in the world. The pace of installation has increased 3.2 times over the last nine months, rising from 5,038 installations a day in October 2025 to nearly 16,328 installations a day in July 2026.
July 2026 alone recorded 5.06 lakh households benefited, the highest ever monthly figure since the scheme began.
To support this momentum, Rs 28,024 crore in subsidy has been released directly to beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer. As a result, nearly 19 lakh households are now receiving zero electricity bills, significantly easing the financial burden on families. More than 12 lakh households have together earned Rs 421 crore through sale of surplus power in FY 2024-25, translating to an extra income of around Rs 3,500 per year per household for those exporting power back to the grid.
Under the Utility Led Aggregation model, 1.6 lakh installations have been completed for PMAY, BPL and SC/ST households across 4 States, with the model sanctioned for rollout in 12 States. The model is enabling low-income households to access rooftop solar while helping States reduce their tariff subsidy burden. Concessional loans at 5.75 percent, benchmarked to the Repo rate plus 50 basis points, have been sanctioned for 21.87 lakh applicants, of which 17.5 lakh installations have already been completed through loan financing, with Jan Samarth integration enabling paperless loan processing.
The scheme has also created a wide vendor and employment ecosystem, with 34,219 registered vendors, of whom 29,469 are active, operating across the country. Over 2.32 lakh people have been trained under capacity building programmes supporting the rooftop solar value chain. Cumulatively, 14.8 GW of rooftop solar capacity has been commissioned under the scheme so far.

Government Boosts MSME Financing Through SIDBI and ECLGS 5.0
articles.full_content:
SIDBI Expands Nationwide Presence with 71 New Branches; Direct Credit Portfolio Grows 36.8% Y-oY ECLGS 5.0 Envisages ₹2.55 Lakh Crore Additional Credit With up to 100% Guarantee Coverage for Eligible MSMEs
Some major initiatives have been undertaken by Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) during the last five years to improve the flow of credit to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) across the country.
These include the following initiatives:
• Subsequent to Union Budget Announcement FY 2024-25, SIDBI has opened 71 new branches across India from 01.04.2024 to 29.07.2026 to expand its reach to serve major MSME clusters and provide direct credit to MSMEs.
• As on March 31, 2026, SIDBI’s direct credit outstanding portfolio stands at ₹ 51,687 crores, as against ₹ 37,781 crores as on 31 March, 2025, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 36.8%.
• The Bank also provides refinance assistance to augment resources of Primary Lending Institutions (PLIs) to increase their flow of credit to MSMEs. As on March 31, 2026, SIDBI’s refinance outstanding portfolio stands at ₹ 4,50,571 crore, as against ₹ 3,85,327 crore as on 31 March, 2025, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 16.9%.
• SIDBI has launched a product on co-lending arrangement with Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) to provide affordable credit to smaller MSMEs, especially new borrowers, as part of its effort to reach underserved/ unserved MSMEs. During FY 202526, the Bank initiated co-lending arrangements with Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) to strengthen credit delivery and broaden financial access in underserved and untapped areas.
• Prayaas Scheme has been launched by SIDBI to facilitate access to affordable credit to informal micro-entrepreneurs/ micro-enterprises (IMEs), especially women and poor.
• SIDBI has launched a GST Sahay app for ‘on tap’ invoice-based (cash flow based) small value credit to micro enterprises using trade data and digital frameworks.
The Government has introduced Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 in May, 2026. Under the scheme, MSMEs are eligible for additional credit up to 20% of the peak fund-based working capital outstanding during the fourth quarter of FY 2025–26.
The scheme provides 100% guarantee coverage to Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) towards the amount in default for such additional credit facility extended to the eligible MSME borrowers. For the scheduled passenger airlines, the guarantee coverage is 90%.
However, the scheduled passenger airlines are eligible for additional credit up to 100% of the total peak credit outstanding (both fund-based and non-fund-based) during the fourth quarter of FY 2025-26. Under the scheme, additional credit flow of ₹ 2,55,000 crore is envisaged for MSMEs, non-MSMEs and scheduled passenger airlines.
This information was given by Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance Shri Pankaj Chaudhary in Rajya Sabha today.

articles.full_content:
The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Shillong, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in collaboration with National Law University (NLU) Meghalaya and support of the three professional institutes—ICAI (lead co-host), ICSI (support co-host), and ICMAI(support co-host)—hosted a strategic webinar for promotion of the Corporate Mitra Scheme in Meghalaya. The webinar aimed to create awareness about the Corporate Mitra Scheme and its role in developing a skilled workforce and enhancing employability among the youth of Meghalaya, as part of the ongoing Northeast awareness campaign.
The Corporate Mitra Scheme, announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, aims to empower MSMEs, primarily within Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities – thereby strengthening the business ecosystem, by establishing a network of trained and accredited Corporate Mitras. The initiative further consolidates the efforts of the Government towards a resilient, inclusive, and formalized MSME sector that drives sustainable economic growth and job creation. The initiative directly aligns with the Government of India’s vision of a Viksit Bharat @ 2047 by fostering entrepreneurship and promoting the ease of doing business. The initiative is designed to addresses critical capacity gaps by building a dedicated cadre of local paraprofessionals known as "Corporate Mitras", who will assist Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) with essential regulatory and compliance frameworks - allowing businesses to optimize growth while creating sustainable career pathways for regional youth. The “Corporate Mitra” shall function as trusted para-professionals who bridge the gap between complex regulatory compliance and commercial development, by providing accessible and affordable support services, thereby ensuring that smaller enterprises are able to navigate administrative and compliance aspects with ease.
To build this network, the government focuses on equipping young graduates with industry-relevant knowledge and practical skills, thereby transforming them into a career-ready cadre of business support professionals capable of delivering high-quality professional assistance. Consequently, the program creates new professional employment pathways while simultaneously upgrading the quality of support available to local businesses. Accredited Corporate Mitras shall be equipped with requisite skillset and competency to handle non-core operations, including financial, taxation, accounting, governance, and regulatory needs of enterprises and small businesses. Outsourcing these tedious tasks allows local enterprises to meet all necessary legal requirements with complete ease. As a result, MSME owners can confidently redirect their focus toward core business drivers like innovation, expansion, and long-term scaling.

Government is actively working to expand training opportunities across the country including in rural, tribal, and aspirational districts, by encouraging more training infrastructure, better coverage of underserved areas, and strengthening of skilling initiatives through the State Skill Development Missions.
An independent third-party impact evaluation of the PMKVY 4.0 was conducted by Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of India. As per the report, PMKVY training has contributed to a measurable shift in employment outcomes for short term training (STT) candidates. The combined share of employed and self-employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 percentage point increase. Income- related outcomes also show positive movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) candidates reporting an increase in income following training and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded access to formal skill training and certification and has generated measurable improvements in skill confidence, employment participation, and income outcomes for a substantial proportion of beneficiaries.
Further, various processes have been put in place under PMKVY across the training lifecycle to ensure enrolled candidates receive quality training in compliance with PMKVY guidelines. Researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bhilai have developed an innovative technology to transform discarded Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) plastic bottles into a high-value engineering material that can be reshaped, repaired and recycled repeatedly. The breakthrough is expected to provide a sustainable solution to plastic waste management while strengthening circular economy practices and supporting next-generation manufacturing technologies, including three-dimensional (3D) printing.
The research was led by Dr. Sanjib Banerjee of the Department of Chemistry, Indian Institute of Technology Bhilai, with researchers Priyank Sinha, Bharatbhushan Meshram and Onkarnath Verma. The findings have been published in the internationally reputed journal Materials Today Catalysis, underscoring the institute's growing contribution to sustainable materials research. The team has also filed an Indian patent application for the technology.
Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) is one of the world's most widely used plastics, particularly in beverage bottles and food packaging, generating millions of tonnes of waste annually. Although PET is recyclable, conventional recycling processes gradually degrade the quality of the material, limiting its long-term reuse and value. To overcome this challenge, the researchers developed a green, magnetically recoverable catalyst using waste eucalyptus leaves. The catalyst efficiently converts discarded Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) bottles into a valuable chemical building block and can be easily separated using a magnet for repeated reuse. This makes the depolymerisation process cleaner, more sustainable and cost-effective. The recovered building block is subsequently converted into a high-performance dynamic polymer that combines mechanical strength with reprocessability and offers significant potential for future three-dimensional (3D) printing applications. The technology effectively transforms discarded plastic bottles from an environmental liability into high-value engineering materials, demonstrating a practical "waste-to-wealth" approach. By reducing plastic waste, lowering dependence on virgin petroleum-based raw materials and enabling repeated reuse instead of disposal, the innovation has the potential to significantly reduce the environmental and carbon footprint associated with plastic products. It also reinforces the transition towards sustainable manufacturing and a circular economy. A key feature of the newly developed material is its ability to soften when heated, be reshaped into a desired form and permanently retain the new shape upon cooling.
